title: Ari (Chas McIvor)
style: Afro-folk acoustic guitar warm female vocal storytelling 100bpm brushed drums light honest character portrait child singer Australian family unhurried hopeful
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, light and wide, morning feel]
Ten years old.
Sang in front of one of Joel's mates.
He used to run the venue.
Had all the bands in.
He said: wow.

[Verse 1]
She had a head cold that day
And she still stopped the room
The kind of singer who doesn't have to try
Because trying is already in them
Oma told Joel
You have to breathe when you sing
Joel was trying
He just couldn't
Ari doesn't have that problem
She breathes and the room holds still

[Verse 2]
Joel texted at midnight:
Ari is the best singer in the house
She will be famous
That's her dad saying that
Not a manager
Not a label
Her dad
Who knows what famous sounds like
From the inside of a family
And called it anyway
At midnight
Going to bed

[Chorus]
Ari
Ten years old
Ari
The room went quiet
Ari
Joel's daughter
Ari
With a head cold
Ari
And still the best one there
Ari
She will be famous
Her dad said so
At midnight
Ari

[Bridge - spoken, warm and unhurried]
Oma said: Nay Joel, you have to breathe when you sing.
He was trying. He just couldn't.
The nose wasn't working right.
Got it fixed eventually.
And he can breathe now.
Ari never had that problem.
She breathes like she was built for this.
Because she was.
Ari.
Ten.
Going somewhere.

[Chorus reprise]
Ari
Best singer in the house
Ari
Joel's girl
Ari
She will be famous
Ari

[Outro - guitar alone, simple and sure]
When you're ready, Ari.
The vault is open.
The tracks are waiting.
Joel already called it.
At midnight.
Going to bed.
